Improving moisture stability via Cs2PtI6 5.1 Introduction           Notable achievements in organic–inorganic halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have been made recently due to their tunable bandgaps, high absorption coefficients, fast bipolar charge transport, long electron–hole diffusion, and easy preparation process.1-5 To date, the highest certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of PSCs is 25.5%, comparable to that of traditional Si-based solar cells.6 However, device stability still restrict the commercialization PSCs because of organic components, such as CH3NH3+ (MA+) and HC(NH2)2+ (FA+) ions, which are hygroscopic and volatile under humid, light, and hot conditions.7-10 Therefore, developing volatile-free all-inorganic perovskite materials, such as CsPbX3 (X = I, Br, and Cl or their mixtures), is an efficient strategy.

Among inorganic perovskites, CsPbX3-based PSCs demonstrate superior photoelectric performance and thermal stability.11, 12 Among CsPbX3 materials, α-CsPbI3 has the most proper bandgap (approximately 1.73 eV) but is easily converted to δ-CsPbI3 with a bandgap of 2.82 eV at room temperature; this feature does not take full advantage of visible light.13 By contrast, CsPbBr3 is stable at room temperature, but its wide bandgap (2.34 eV) limits light absorption and utilization.
As a member of the CsPbX3 family, CsPbI2Br with a bandgap of 1.91 eV has become the most promising absorber layer, making a trade-off between efficiency and stability.
In recent years, various strategies have been applied to highly efficient CsPbI2Br-based PSCs, such as of ion doping,14-16 interface modification,17-19 and developing hole transfer layer.

20-22 To date, the efficiency of CsPbI2Br-based PSCs has exceeded 17%, with a traditional device architecture of conductive substrate/electron transfer layer (ETL)/perovskite/HTL/Au, exhibiting a brilliant development prospect.
